reason: Write n=db and m=da with gcd(a,b)=1. Then km modulo n is always d times the residue of ka modulo b, and as k runs from 1 to n each residue modulo b occurs exactly d times. Therefore the residues r_k are the multiples of d, each repeated d times. For j, the condition r_k≥j is equivalent to the smaller residue being at least ceil(j/d), giving |S_{m,j}|=d(b-ceil(j/d))≤db-j=n-j.
